overview: The committee approved the adoption of a new unified middle school math curriculum and a resolution calling on the state to exempt students from MCAS requirements due to a racist exam question. Members also heard presentations on phasing out styrofoam trays, adolescent cannabis research, and the district's breakfast program.

items.title: Routine Business
items.summary: Approved the minutes from May 6, 2019, along with bills, payrolls, and the transfer of funds.

items.title: Proposal to Phase Out Styrofoam Trays
items.summary: Approved a motion to study the cost and feasibility of replacing single-use styrofoam lunch trays with reusable or biodegradable options following a presentation by parents and students.

items.title: Middle School String Ensemble Recognition
items.summary: Recognized the Medford Middle School String Ensemble for earning a Medal of Excellence at the Massachusetts Instrumental and Chorus Conductors Association Music Festival.

items.title: ELA MCAS Performance Analysis
items.summary: Discussed disparities in 2018 ELA MCAS results across elementary schools and the impact of student demographics on achievement targets.

items.title: Teacher Morale and Literacy Instruction
items.summary: Member Paul Ruseau apologized for disparaging remarks made at a previous meeting, after which Medford Teachers Association representatives defended the district's phonics instruction and advocated for increased professional development funding.

items.title: Citywide Elementary PTO Annual Update
items.summary: Representatives from the four elementary school parent organizations presented their annual reports and detailed the success of their new citywide fundraising alliance.

items.title: Universal Free Breakfast Presentation
items.summary: Project Bread presented the 'Provision 2' model for offering universal free breakfast district-wide, leading the committee to request a formal financial feasibility report for the June 17th meeting.

items.title: Adolescent Cannabis Research Study
items.summary: Dr. Randy Schuster of Massachusetts General Hospital proposed a research study involving local students to understand and reduce adolescent cannabis use through abstinence incentives.

items.title: Middle School Math Curriculum Adoption
items.summary: Approved the adoption of 'Illustrative Math' as the unified middle school curriculum and allocated $6,500 for initial professional development despite teacher concerns regarding the lack of physical textbooks.

items.title: Resolution on Racist MCAS Question
items.summary: Approved a resolution calling on the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education to exempt 10th graders from graduation requirements due to a racist essay question on the English exam.
